name: Tomato
description: A popular vegetable plant that grows easily at home and produces fresh, juicy tomatoes. Perfect for beginners and great for sunny balconies or gardens.
growthSteps: Select healthy tomato seeds from a trusted source
Soak seeds in water for 6–8 hours to improve germination
Prepare seed tray with moist potting soil
Plant seeds 1 cm deep and cover lightly with soil
Water gently and keep in warm, sunny location
Wait for seedlings to grow 5–10 cm tall
Transfer seedlings to larger pots or garden bed
Continue watering and provide support as plant grows

name: Basil
description: A fragrant herb used in cooking that thrives indoors or outdoors. Easy to grow and adds fresh flavor to your kitchen.
growthSteps: Choose fresh basil seeds or buy seedlings
Fill small pot with moist potting soil
Sprinkle seeds on soil surface and press gently
Cover pot loosely with plastic wrap for humidity
Place in warm spot with indirect sunlight
Remove covering once seedlings appear
Water when top soil feels dry to touch
Harvest leaves regularly to encourage bushier growth

name: Pothos (Devil's Ivy)
description: A low-maintenance indoor plant with trailing vines and heart-shaped leaves. Perfect for beginners and works well in low light.
sunlight: Bright indirect light, tolerates low light
growthTime: No germination needed, grows from cuttings in 2–3 weeks
growthSteps: Obtain healthy pothos cuttings from an existing plant
Cut stems 4–6 inches below a leaf node
Remove lower leaves to expose the nodes
Place cuttings in water jar or pot with moist soil
Keep in warm location with indirect light
Change water every 2–3 days if propagating in water
Wait for roots to develop over 2–3 weeks
Transfer rooted cuttings to soil and maintain steady moisture

name: Sunflower
description: A tall, cheerful flower that produces large blooms and seeds. Great outdoor plant that attracts pollinators to your garden.
watering: Regular watering, let soil dry between waterings
growthSteps: Choose large, healthy sunflower seeds
Plant seeds directly in garden, 1.5 inches deep
Space seeds 6 inches apart in rows
Water soil gently after planting
Keep soil consistently moist until seedlings emerge
Thin seedlings to 12 inches apart once they're 4 inches tall
Water deeply once a week from seedling stage onward
Stake tall varieties for support and watch blooms appear

name: Mint
description: A hardy aromatic herb with refreshing flavor, great for tea and cooking. Grows quickly and can spread, so container growing is recommended.
sunlight: Partial shade to partial sun (4–6 hours)
growthSteps: Get mint seeds or healthy plant cuttings
Fill pot with moist potting soil
Press seeds lightly onto soil surface or insert cuttings
Cover pot with plastic wrap to retain moisture
Place in warm location with indirect light
Keep soil moist but not soggy
Remove cover once seedlings sprout
Begin harvesting leaves once plant is 4-6 inches tall

name: Spider Plant
description: A popular indoor plant with long, striped leaves and small flower-like plantlets. Very hardy and produces baby plants naturally.
watering: Water when top inch of soil is dry
growthTime: No germination, grows from plantlets in 1–2 weeks
growthSteps: Obtain spider plant babies (plantlets) from a mature plant
Separate babies gently with small roots attached
Prepare small pot with moist potting soil
Plant babies at same depth as original, roots in soil
Place in bright, indirect light
Water gently to settle soil around roots
Keep soil consistently moist for first 2 weeks
Once established, maintain regular watering schedule

name: Lettuce
description: A cool-season leafy vegetable that grows quickly. Perfect for container gardening and provides fresh salad leaves within weeks.
growthSteps: Choose loose-leaf or butter lettuce seeds
Prepare seed tray with moist soil
Sprinkle seeds thinly on soil surface
Press seeds gently and cover lightly with soil
Keep soil moist and place in cool, bright location
Thin seedlings to 6 inches apart once they're 2 inches tall
Transplant to larger container or garden bed
Start harvesting outer leaves when plant is 3-4 inches tall

name: Aloe Vera
description: A succulent plant with medicinal gel inside leaves. Requires minimal care and water, perfect for sunny windowsills.
watering: Water sparingly, let soil dry completely
growthTime: No germination needed, established plants for best results
growthSteps: Obtain aloe vera pup or cutting from mature plant
Let cutting dry for 2–3 days before planting
Prepare pot with cactus soil mix
Plant cutting 1–2 inches deep in soil
Do not water for first week to allow roots to develop
Place in bright, sunny location
Water lightly once a month during growing season
Harvest gel-filled leaves as needed for use

name: Chili Pepper
description: A spicy vegetable plant that produces colorful peppers. Great for growing outdoors and provides fresh peppers for cooking.
watering: Water when soil surface is dry
growthTime: 10–14 days germination, 2–3 months to first peppers
growthSteps: Select quality chili pepper seeds suited to your climate
Start seeds indoors in seed tray with warm conditions
Plant seeds 1 cm deep in moist soil
Maintain consistent warmth and moisture for germination
Once seedlings are 3 inches tall, transplant to larger pots
Harden off seedlings by gradually exposing to outdoor conditions
Plant in garden in full sun once weather is warm
Water regularly and stake plants as they grow taller

name: Lavender
description: A fragrant flowering plant with purple blooms and aromatic leaves. Attracts butterflies and bees to your garden.
watering: Low watering, drought tolerant once established
growthTime: 14–21 days germination, 2–3 months to first blooms
growthSteps: Obtain lavender seeds or cuttings from existing plant
Fill seed tray with well-draining sandy soil mix
Place seeds on soil surface, press lightly, do not cover
Mist soil lightly and keep in warm location
Wait 2–3 weeks for seeds to germinate
Once seedlings have 2–3 leaves, transplant to larger pots
Harden off seedlings for outdoor planting
Plant in garden and water minimally once established
